# Walkthrough — Corporate Controller, disbursement and statements

Date: 2026-06-09
Present: Corporate Controller (Corinne Baptiste), Treasury Analyst
(Renata Kowalczyk), engagement lead

## The Friday run

"The AP Manager sends me the proposal as an Excel export Thursday
afternoon. I look at anything over twenty-five thousand line by line, and I
look at any new payee regardless of amount. Then I reply approving it."

Asked where the approved export is filed: "It's in my mail. I couldn't tell
you if it gets saved anywhere formal — treasury works from the NetSuite run,
not from my copy." Retention location for the approved proposal could not be
established during the walkthrough.

"Treasury builds the NACHA file out of NetSuite and uploads it in Chase
Connect. Renata uploads, I release. Separate user IDs, separate tokens —
that has been true since the bank set us up."

Treasury Analyst: "I take the cash position sheet into the run too. If
we're tight I'll tell the AP Manager to pull a few off and we do them the
following week."

## Statements

"Statement reconciliation is in the SOP but I've never audited that it
happens for anything but the top vendors. The worksheets are supposed to
live on the shared drive under Finance. I have not looked."

## Where invoice capture belongs

"Capture exceptions I'd frankly call a document management problem, not an
AP problem — the SOP says the same thing. The AP Manager treats them as
part of her invoice handling because she's the one who feels them. Both
views are defensible; we've never settled it."
